blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Long before container ships and cargo planes shrank the world, massive wooden galleons were already crossing the Pacific, linking Manila and Acapulco and connecting Asia with the Americas. For nearly 250 years, the ships carried silk, spices and other Asian goods to Mexico, returning with American silver. But the Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade carried more than cargo. People, ideas and cultures traveled with the ships, turning the Philippines into a crossroads of a rapidly connected world. Today, that chapter of history is being brought to life at Museo del Galeón, a four-level maritime museum at the SM Mall of Asia […]...
